title: RONI gave no clear gain over ONI for the Atlantic to Pacific cyclone energy ratio in 2002-2025
abstract: We tested whether observed August-October RONI gave smaller later-year errors than ONI for the log ratio of Atlantic to northeast and central Pacific tropical-stage cyclone energy. We used shared NOAA HURDAT2 and ERSST version 5 index tables for 1982-2025. Models with an index and a time trend were fitted on earlier years and tested in 2002-2025. Mean squared error was 0.999 for RONI and 0.930 for ONI. ONI minus RONI error was -0.0693, with an approximate three-year block interval of -0.1870 to 0.0279. Without the time trend, the point result favored RONI. All planned three-year sensitivity intervals included zero. Thus, this test gives no clear index advantage that holds across the tested model choices. The outcome excludes subtropical stages. The study uses observed same-season indices and revised tracks, not archived forecasts. The short record, climate reference differences, rounding, observation changes and unmeasured drivers limit inference. Code, annual evidence, exact source hashes, all test errors and an independent audit are included.

display.caption: Left: ASO RONI and the log tropical-stage ACE ratio in 1982-2025; colors run from early purple to late yellow. Center: observed and sequential model values in 2002-2025. Right: paired MSE differences with approximate three-year block intervals. Positive values favor RONI. All shown intervals include zero. Pacific includes northeast and central Pacific records.
